| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v3 | In a Hilbert-space model only unitarily invariant structure is intrinsic; a basis or tensor factorisation, and so any parts or features, is extra data supplied from outside the space, and the record's Hilbert-space works differ in where they get it | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. | [THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md) v2 | Symmetry forces spectral degeneracy but degeneracy does not identify a symmetry: an operator commuting with a group has eigenspaces built from its real irreducibles, so abelian rotation groups force pairs over ℝ, and the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside a multiplet | Peter & Weyl (1927), [LIT-329](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-329.md) §3, build representations as eigenspaces of an invariant kernel, and Kondor & Trivedi, [LIT-305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-305.md) Lemma 6, show that intertwiners preserve isotypic components. It adds the real-scalar correction in [NOTE-282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-282.md), found in the reading of [LIT-362](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-362.md), and the counting in the reading of [LIT-346](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-346.md). It does not support "degeneracy detects symmetry": a spectrum is consistent with several groups and says nothing about the characters inside a multiplet. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | Every Boolean algebra is the clopen algebra of its Stone space of prime ideals, and a finite one is the power set of its atoms, so a single Boolean context always has two-valued valuations and the Kochen–Specker obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. Kochen & Specker ([LIT-298](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-298.md), Thm 0) turn this into the criterion that a partial Boolean algebra embeds in a Boolean one iff its two-valued homomorphisms separate points. The joining of the two, that non-classicality needs more than one context, is the record's. Neither Stone paper uses "ultrafilter" or states a duality of categories. | Active |
| [THEORY-021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-021.md) | In the efficiently packed geometries of uniform superposition the features form a rank-one POVM compressed from the n-feature basis: their dimensionality-weighted projectors sum to the identity | Elhage et al. (2022), [LIT-323](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-323.md), found that features in uniform superposition settle into polytopes and tegum products, with feature dimensionalities clustering at 3/4, 2/3, 1/2, 2/5 and 3/8. The tight-frame and POVM reading is the reader's inference in [NOTE-278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-278.md), checked numerically there. It was refined when filing: a tegum product is not globally tight, but the Dᵢ-weighted POVM still sums to the identity. None of this is in the paper. It does not make superposition contextual or quantum, and it says nothing yet about trained real models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md) v3 | The reverse-engineered grokking network computes modular addition by multiplying characters of ℤ/p at a few frequencies, the same real two-dimensional irreducibles later found as circles in language models; in both the group comes from the task, not the network | Nanda et al. The reading in terms of characters and irreducibles is [NOTE-283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-283.md)'s, joined here to Engels et al.'s circles ([LIT-322](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-322.md)). | [THEORY-027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md) | Two individually decisive people, weak Pareto and an unrestricted domain cannot all hold, even when choice need only yield a best element; unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability | Sen (1970), [LIT-285](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-285.md): no social decision function satisfies U, weak Pareto and minimal liberalism. The proof was checked in this record, including the unproved one-way strengthening. Sen (1998), [LIT-282](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-282.md): the paradox, unlike Arrow's, is not resolved by interpersonal comparisons. The theorem is settled. Whether pairwise decisiveness is what liberty is remains open, and the record reads the rights-as-game-forms literature only through Sen's reply to it. | Active |
| [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) | The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). The ROC's slope equals the threshold (Thm 8). Tanner & Swets (1954), [LIT-368](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md), carry this over to the human observer as d′ plus a criterion. Stanislaw & Todorov (1999), [LIT-367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md), state that d′ varies with the criterion unless the variances are equal. The separation of sensitivity from bias is a property of the model, not of the data. | Active |
| [THEORY-032](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-032.md) | The Yoneda lemma determines an object only up to isomorphism, from its whole hom-functor, among objects the category already has; as a formal version of "an object is determined by its relations" it presupposes the relata | nLab, Yoneda lemma (rev. 2026-08-17), [LIT-221](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md) — y is fully faithful and y(c) ≅ y(d) iff c ≅ d, and pointwise bijections of hom-sets without naturality do not suffice. Lam & Wüthrich ([LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md)) state two of its consequences without the name. The philosophical reading, a relational criterion of identity up to isomorphism rather than a construction of objects from relations, is the record's own. It does not say that the lemma supports eliminating objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md) | In the topos programme quantum propositions form a distributive Heyting algebra, not an orthocomplemented lattice, and its negation is a pseudo-complement under which excluded middle can fail | Döring & Isham (2007, II), [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md) — daseinisation maps each projector injectively to a clopen sub-object of the spectral presheaf, with δ(P∨Q) = δ(P)∨δ(Q) but only δ(P∧Q) ⪯ δ(P)∧δ(Q). The orthocomplement is carried to inner daseinisation, not to ¬δ(P). That Sub_cl(Σ) is Heyting (Thm 2.5) is sketched: implication is not written out and the laws are not checked. Paper I ([LIT-343](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md)) chooses intuitionistic deduction. Isham–Butterfield ([LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md)) state that the Heyting algebra is fixed by the base category. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-038.md) | Category theory gives radical ontic structural realism no formal support: generalized elements exist in every category, morphisms relate objects the category presupposes, and Bain's physical cases eliminate spacetime points, not relata | Lam & Wüthrich (2015), [LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md), against Bain (2013), [LIT-223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md). Bain's "structure as object in a category" relabels relata rather than removing them, and his GR and TQFT cases dispose of points only. That the Yoneda lemma ([LIT-221](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md)) strengthens the rebuttal is the record's inference: no paper in the debate names it. This does not refute radical OSR. It removes one argument for it, and Eva 2016's reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-041.md) | Birkhoff and von Neumann proposed the modular law, not orthomodularity, and proved it fails for closed subspaces in infinite dimension; Husimi used the orthomodular identity only as an unnamed proof step | Birkhoff & von Neumann (1936), [LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md) — the lattice of closed subspaces is orthocomplemented and not distributive. They propose modularity (L5), motivated by a dimension function, and give an explicit infinite-dimensional pentagon that breaks it. The word "orthomodular" does not occur. Husimi (1937), [LIT-357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-357.md), derives modularity as the parallelogram law under a finite-chain assumption and uses the orthomodular identity as a step without naming it. Citing either paper for "the orthomodular lattice of quantum logic" misattributes it. | Active |
| [THEORY-042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-042.md) | Under a superselection rule a coherent superposition across sectors is operationally a mixture, because no observable connects the sectors; Wick, Wightman and Wigner proved such a rule for integer versus half-integer spin and only postulated it for charge | Wick, Wightman & Wigner (1952), [LIT-339](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-339.md) — they define a superselection rule and show that a superposition across sectors "is not a pure state, but a statistical mixture". They prove the rule from time reversal for integer versus half-integer angular momentum, and postulate it for charge with "no conclusive evidence". What follows for Birkhoff–von Neumann's lattice ([LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md)), a product of sector lattices with central sector projections, is the record's inference. The centre-of-the-algebra formulation belongs to Haag, who is not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md) | Steepest descent is defined only relative to a metric, and Amari's proof that natural-gradient learning is Fisher efficient needs the Fisher information at the optimum to be invertible, the condition whose failure WBIC calls singular; in a multilayer perceptron it fails wherever an output weight is zero | Amari (1998), [LIT-607](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-607.md). Theorem 1 is a Lagrangian derivation: under \|dw\|² = Σg_ij dw_i dw_j the steepest-descent direction is −G⁻¹∇L, so it changes with G. Theorem 2 shows that online learning with step 1/t along the Fisher natural gradient attains the Cramér–Rao bound G⁻¹/t, and its proof uses G(w*)⁻¹. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), Eq. 14, calls a truth regular when the optimum is one point and its Fisher is positive definite, and singular otherwise. From Amari's own Eq. 6.12, the score for hidden unit i's input weights carries the factor v_i. So the Fisher of a multilayer perceptron loses rank wherever an output weight is zero. That set is part of the optimum whenever the teacher needs fewer hidden units than the student has. Active because each step is checkable in the two texts. The claim that the Fisher is the only invariant metric is Chentsov's, cited and not held. | Active |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) v2 | Because the Gauss–Newton Fisher JᵀJ and the NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ share their non-zero spectrum, the lazy-regime Fisher of a ReLU network on spherical data inherits the NTK's harmonic-degree blocks, and a spectral threshold on it is well posed only at gaps between blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md) | In the kernel regime gradient descent fits the target eigenspace by eigenspace of the neural tangent kernel, at rates set by their eigenvalues; on uniform spherical data the eigenspaces are the harmonic degrees, and for fully connected ReLU networks the non-zero eigenvalues decay as k^(−d) at every depth | Three derived results that compose. Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md), Theorem 4.2: for a wide two-layer ReLU network, the training residual's component in the top-r_k NTK eigenspace falls as (1 − λ_{r_k})^T, for any target. Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md): on uniform spherical data the Gram matrix is a convolution, so its eigenvectors are harmonics, with closed-form eigenvalues per frequency. The bias-free kernel is zero on odd frequencies k ≥ 3, and a bias restores them. Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md), Corollary 3: the L-layer ReLU NTK decays as k^(−d) on S^(d−1), the same exponent at every depth. Active for the kernel regime on uniform spherical data, where every step is proved. It says nothing about networks whose kernel moves. | Active |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) | The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold and falls below d/2 when the prior is positive on the optimal set | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is derived. The singular half is a theorem the record holds only as cited, so this is Proposed. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-106.md) | In random-features ridge regression the double-descent peak is a divergence of the test error at the interpolation threshold 2N = n as the ridge goes to zero, which a positive ridge keeps finite and a ridge of the tuned size removes; minimum-norm linear regression has the same peak at n = d in exact finite-sample form | Liao, Couillet & Mahoney (2020), [LIT-679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md): for random Fourier features with n, p and N large together, the test MSE has a closed form through a deterministic equivalent of the resolvent. As λ → 0 its corrections jump from O(1) to order 1/λ across 2N = n, det(Ω⁻¹) scales as λ, and the test error diverges at 2N = n unless the test data lie within about λ of the training data. At λ = 10⁻⁷ and 10⁻³ the curve has a singular peak; at the tuned λ ≈ 0.2 and at 10 it has none. Dereziński, Liang & Mahoney (2019), [LIT-683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-683.md): exact MSE of the minimum-norm estimator under a surrogate design, peaking at n = d with value σ² tr(Σ⁻¹), and below the threshold equal in expectation to ridge regression at the λn that makes the ridge effective dimension n. Proportional-limit theorems for one shallow model each; nothing here reaches trained deep networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) | Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time | Aubin's viability theory, read in his 1999 mini-course notes [LIT-714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-714.md). Given dynamics and a set K of required states, K is viable if some evolution from each state stays in K and invariant if every one does. Nagumo's theorem reduces viability to a tangency condition. The viability kernel is the largest viable subset of K; from outside it every evolution exits K. The notes do not compare viability with stability; that contrast is a further step. | Active |
| [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. The direction from simulation to informativeness is Blackwell (1951); the finite converse is Sherman and Stein (1951); the general converse is proved in 1953. It is a qualitative order and says nothing about how much worse an incomparable experiment is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | The classical theorems on sufficient statistics need only the copy/discard structure of Markov kernels: Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need only strict positivity, not the existence of conditional distributions | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-158](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md) | In a Markov process, an observable commutes with the generator exactly when its mean and variance are both conserved in every state; on a finite state space this means it is constant on each connected component of the transition graph, so a conserved mean alone does not give a symmetry | Baez & Fong (2013), [LIT-773](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-773.md), read in [NOTE-598](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-598.md): Theorem 1 (finite state space, four equivalent conditions) and Theorems 2–3 (σ-finite measure spaces, without the component form). Unlike quantum mechanics, where a mean conserved in every state already implies commutation, a Markov process can conserve the mean of an observable it does not commute with. The theorem covers diagonal observables only; it says nothing about symmetries that permute states. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md) | In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators | Baez (2020), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md), read in [NOTE-630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-630.md), Theorems 3, 4, 8 and 10, with Alfsen and Shultz's theorem quoted as Theorem 12. With unique solutions to the flow equations, "a generates symmetries of b iff b generates symmetries of a" is {a, b} = 0 ⇔ {b, a} = 0. It assumes reversible one-parameter groups and an observable–generator map; it says nothing about dissipative or stochastic dynamics, nor about the Lagrangian form of Noether's theorem. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a convex, piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table | From Abramsky, Barbosa & Mansfield (2017), [LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md): the non-contextual fraction is the value of a linear programme whose constraint vector is the empirical model (Eq. 3), and convexity of CF under mixing is their Theorem 2. Piecewise linearity and the Lipschitz bound are the reader's derivation from strong duality, not stated in the paper. The Lipschitz constant depends on the scenario and is not bounded here. Nothing here applies to signalling data, where CF is undefined. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) | In Contextuality-by-Default, whether a fixed set of measurements is contextual depends on how the system is represented: which couplings are imposed, and which dichotomizations of the variables are included | Dzhafarov, Cervantes & Kujala (2017), [LIT-790](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-790.md), with Dzhafarov & Kujala's CbD 2.0 ([LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md)) and CbD 1.0 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md)). The same measurements can receive different verdicts. Maximal and multimaximal couplings disagree when a content appears in three or more contexts. Multimaximal couplings of non-binary variables can be destroyed by coarse-graining. With every dichotomization kept, two content-sharing variables are contextual on their own unless one nominally dominates the other. The authors present the representation as the analyst's choice, not as a defect. What the record does not get from these papers is any rule for choosing it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v2 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf. It is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event ("solipsistic contextuality"), and so always when the space is tight, as every space induced by a causal order is. The non-gluing example was checked here; the general theorem's proof was not read. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) | Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). A simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Along any simulation the non-contextual fraction cannot fall; contextual models cannot be cloned; and which maps between model sets are simulations is a non-contextuality question on a hom scenario. No-signalling models only, and nothing about information preserved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md) | In a tied single-head attention layer trained by ridge-penalized empirical risk minimization on high-dimensional Gaussian sequences, weight decay is a nuclear-norm penalty on the query–key map, and the learned map is a soft-thresholded noisy copy of the target: its outliers are recovered target directions and its bulk is finite-sample noise | Boncoraglio, Erba, Troiani, Xu, Krzakala & Zdeborová (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md): with S = WWᵀ, λ‖W‖²_F is exactly λ‖S‖_* (Appendix A), and in the limit n/d², p/d fixed the trained WᵀW/√(pd) has the law η·ReLU(S0 + δZ − εI), Z ∼ GOE, with δ a noise level that falls with the data and ε a threshold set by λ (Claim 4.1, replica/AMP, checked against Adam at d ≤ 400). It does not say that real transformers' spectra arise this way: the data are isotropic Gaussian, the target is inside the model class, and the agreement with measured spectra is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md) | When the co-occurrence of words on a latent continuum depends only on their separation, a spectral word embedding places them on the Fourier modes of that continuum, so the circles and rippled curves of months, years and places come from a symmetry of the corpus statistics | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart and Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md): proved for an embedding whose Gram matrix equals the co-occurrence matrix (or its absolute value) at full rank, with the exponential kernel solved for both boundary conditions; the symmetry measured in Wikipedia; matching PCA pictures in Gemma 2. That trained networks get their geometry this way is inferred, not tested: nothing in the paper changes the statistics and watches the geometry follow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-184](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-184.md) | Under a permutation-equivariant update whose map is K-Lipschitz, coincident neurons stay coincident at every step size, and at step size below 1/K distinct neurons cannot merge in finitely many steps | Yang, Poggio, Chuang and Ziyin (2025), [LIT-861](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-861.md), read in [NOTE-663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-663.md). If an update commutes with permuting neurons (GD, SGD or Adam on a permutation-symmetric loss) and its map is K-Lipschitz, one step of size η changes every pairwise neuron distance by a factor in [1 − ηK, 1 + ηK]. This is a proved constraint on trajectories. It does not say that training simplifies above 1/K, that neurons never merge in the limit, or that any scale-dependent shape of the neuron cloud is preserved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md) | Nested angular cones in the Poincaré ball, symmetric about the outward ray with an aperture depending only on the apex's radius, are transitive only if the aperture is at most π/2 and r sin ψ(r)/(1 − r²) does not increase outward; so no such cone can be defined near the origin, the widest admissible family is sin ψ = K(1 − r²)/r, and every point a cone contains lies farther from the origin than its apex | Ganea, Bécigneul and Hofmann (2018), [LIT-866](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-866.md): Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 prove the necessity half under four stated requirements on the cones; the transitivity of the closed-form family (Theorem 4) is asserted without proof; the radial monotonicity is this record's derivation from the hyperbolic law of cosines. It says what a cone order on the ball can be, not which posets embed in it, and nothing about meets, joins or learned embeddings. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md) | In natural odour sources, the rank order of correlations between compound concentrations has the Betti-curve signature of points near the boundary of a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a uniform Euclidean cube, and human odour-descriptor profiles have that of a full three-dimensional hyperbolic ball | Zhou, Smith & Sharpee (2018), [LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md): for strawberry, tomato, blueberry and mouse-urine volatiles, and for Dravnieks' perceptual ratings of 127 odorants, clique-topology Betti curves match a 3D hyperbolic model and reject uniform Euclidean cubes of every dimension tried. It does not show a tree in the data, and because the fitted odour model is a thin shell, it does not separate a hyperbolic metric from a sphere in flat space. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md) | Pairwise correlations among rat CA1 place cells have the Betti-curve signature of points sampled uniformly from a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a low-dimensional Euclidean cube, and the fitted radius grows with the logarithm of exploration time | Zhang, Rich, Lee & Sharpee (2022), [LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md): in twelve sessions from three data sets, the rank order of CA1 spike correlations matched uniform samples from a 3D hyperbolic ball and not uniform samples from low-dimensional Euclidean cubes or shuffled data, and the ball's radius rose with log exploration time from seconds to days. It does not show that the metric, as opposed to the distribution of field scales, is hyperbolic, nor that a tree is represented. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-193](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-193.md) | A simplicial complex grown by gluing each new d-simplex to one (d − 1)-face, by a rule that uses no geometry, has a tree as its dual and, with every link taken as equal, is a tiling of hyperbolic d-space by ideal simplices; so hyperbolic network geometry can be the outcome of combinatorial growth rather than its cause, though the curvature comes from the equal-length convention and not from the growth | Bianconi and Rahmede (2017), [LIT-867](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-867.md): the tree dual is immediate and the degree law (geometric for d + s = 1, γ = 2 + 1/(d + s − 1) for d + s > 1) is derived by a master equation; the hyperbolic geometry is a drawing, ideal simplices in the Poincaré ball, with uniqueness asserted. The source itself says unequal link lengths would fit the same complex in a sphere. It does not measure hyperbolicity on the graph, and it does not show real networks grow this way. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) | A finite tree embeds in the hyperbolic plane with worst-case distortion 1 + ε, but because a hyperbolic distance d takes about d bits to write, its coordinates need Θ((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits: logarithmic in the branching, linear in the longest path ℓ, so hyperbolic space is economical for shallow bushy hierarchies and not for deep ones | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). The upper bound is Sarkar's construction with the paper's bit count. The lower bound is proved for H² and one family of trees, with an approximation, and dimension's help is shown only as an upper bound. The cost is a cost of coordinates in a fixed-point model, not of the information in the tree, and it says nothing about Euclidean or linear-direction representations of the same hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md) | For networks of smooth units without biases, one hidden layer needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to approximate the monomial x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ and a deep network O(Σ log rᵢ), so the cost of flattening a polynomial grows exponentially with its degree in distinct variables and not with the number of inputs: products of many inputs separate depths, bounded-degree polynomials do not | Rolnick and Tegmark (2017), [LIT-890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-890.md), Theorems 4.1 to 4.3, extending Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's 2ⁿ for a product ([LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md)). Proved for Taylor matching at the origin with bias-free units; the uniform version's lower bound rests on an unproved step. The flip side, that a polynomial of degree d with c monomials costs one layer at most c·2ᵈ however many inputs it has, is the edge: the separation does not reach the low-order polynomials [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md) calls natural. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-233.md) | CKA and normalized Bures similarity are the Euclidean and the Bures comparison of normalized kernels, and each bounds the other only within a factor set by the kernels' ranks, so agreement in one does not carry to the other with a dimension-free constant | Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), §5 and App. A.3, read in [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md). CKA = 1 − ½‖K_X/‖K_X‖_F − K_Y/‖K_Y‖_F‖²_F, while NBS = 1 − ½B²(K_X/Tr K_X, K_Y/Tr K_Y), with B the Bures distance. They induce the same topology, but CKA/√(r(K_X)r(K_Y)) ≤ NBS² ≤ min[r(K_X), r(K_Y)]·CKA, saturated at rank 1. NBS bounds CKA of the square-root kernels, with equality for commuting kernels. Linear kernels only, and the discrepancy is illustrated on Wishart samples, not trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-234.md) | Two softmax next-token predictors induce the same distribution exactly when their embeddings and unembeddings are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces that enter the logits, with arbitrary distortion off them, so a linear relational property is shared by all such models or none only when it lies in those subspaces | Marconato et al. (2024), [LIT-950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-950.md), read in [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md). For p(y\|s) ∝ exp(f(s)ᵀg(y)) on a shared vocabulary, p_{f,g} = p_{f̃,g̃} iff the models are extended-linearly equivalent: invertible linear maps between the subspaces M and N that enter the logits, at any dimensions and without the diversity condition (Thm 5). The dimension of M is then a property of the distribution. Relational linearity, linear subspaces and linear probing hold in all equivalent models or none when Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M (Thm 14), and parallelism is shared only within N (Thm 15). Exact equality of distributions only, and no experiments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md) | A representational similarity index that is invariant to every invertible linear map takes the same value on all representations whose rank equals the number of examples | Kornblith, Norouzi, Lee & Hinton (2019), [LIT-254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-254.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md). If s(X, Z) = s(XA, Z) for every invertible A, and rank(X) = rank(Y) = n, then s(X, Z) = s(Y, Z): any two full-row-rank representations of the same n examples are related by an invertible linear map. So when width reaches the number of examples, an index with that invariance, such as CCA, says nothing. The theorem fixes no group; the paper's case for orthogonal invariance plus isotropic scaling is an argument from training dynamics, not a consequence of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) | For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator are the unique d-dimensional span minimizing worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, with error (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. It does not cover a non-reversible kernel on one space, which the thesis never works through, nor what a trained network reaches. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-247.md) | For finite labelled Markov chains, the discounted bisimulation metric is a bicausal optimal-transport distance, and it equals the value of a finite linear program over occupancy couplings | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2024), [LIT-962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-962.md), read in [NOTE-757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-757.md). For finite action-free chains with real labels r and discount γ, the bisimulation metric's fixed-point equation is the Bellman equation of transport over bicausal couplings with cost (1−γ)\|r(x)−r(y)\|, so the two coincide. The transport cost equals 1/(1−γ) times the minimum of a linear objective over occupancy couplings, under flow and coherence constraints (Lemma 1, Theorem 1). It says nothing of systems with actions. Its link to trace distance is one-way and second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-254.md) | Tangle-defined cohesion matches network communities only where community structure is strongly delineated, and tangles of one to three vertices recur beside the ones that do | Salter-Duke (2024), [LIT-955](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-955.md), a PhD thesis read in full in [NOTE-814](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-814.md). Edge-connectivity tangles, computed exactly at low order on eleven small real networks, give communities close to standard methods where structure is strong (yeast PPI) and none or almost none where it is weak (karate club, C. elegans, college football at the orders reached), and where tangles divide a network some hold only one to three vertices. The relation is read by eye from eight networks, and the vertex sets depend on the author's assignment rule. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md) | Dynamical independence, zero information flow from the microscopic history into a coarse-graining given its own history, fixes emergent macroscopic variables by the dynamics rather than by a chosen query, but generically none is exact and the optima are many | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): definition (2.6), transitivity (App. A), the causal-graph form (2.12), the state-space closed form (3.18) and the genericity count (3.25)–(3.26). The target is the coarse variable's own future, so no outside query is chosen. But the system/environment boundary, the scale and the class of maps are inputs, and the worked theory's candidates are linear subspaces, not partitions. The cost is multimodal, with every local optimum kept. The criterion is closure, not locality or informativeness about a far environment. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-260.md) v3 | An individual string's information splits non-trivially into structure and noise only in a model class without a universal member: with partial recursive models every string's minimal sufficient statistic is trivial, while with total recursive functions it is not, and the finite-set, computable-distribution and total-function classes agree to within logarithmic terms | Vitányi (2001/2006), [LIT-229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-229.md), read in [NOTE-790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-790.md). Sophistication, the shortest model that completes an optimal two-part code, is =⁺ 0 for every string if partial recursive models are allowed (Lemma 6.2). With total recursive models it ranges from about 0 for random strings to above n − log n − 2 log log n for some string of every length (Theorem 6.5), and it agrees with the finite-set and probabilistic versions to within O(log n) (Lemmas 7.1–7.2). It is not computable, and a sufficient-statistic oracle would compute K (Theorems 8.1, 8.3). It says nothing about any computable or learned model. | Active |
| [THEORY-276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md) | In a network of identical units with identical couplings, the orbits of the graph's symmetry group are synchronization clusters, and a cluster moved only by its own factor of the group can lose synchrony while the others keep it | Pecora et al. (2014), [LIT-960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-960.md), read in [NOTE-775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-775.md): eq. (1), the IRR block-diagonalization (eqs. 2–4, 7), the derivation of isolated desynchronization (eq. 6) and an 11-node electro-optic experiment. The pattern of clusters that can synchronize is read from the wiring; whether each does is set by the dynamics through its own transverse block. Symmetry is sufficient, not necessary, for clusters. The paper says nothing about external drive, so the use of these clusters as a sign of coupling rather than a shared cue is the record's inference. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) | For individual data, at every bound on model complexity, the model with the shortest two-part code is, to within O(log n), the best-fitting model in randomness deficiency, although the fit itself cannot be computed or approximated | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-284.md) | If a feature's values form a compact metric space carried continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere, and cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function of squared feature distance, then every path on the representation manifold is √(−2g′(0)) times as long as the feature path it images, so on-manifold shortest paths recover the feature's intrinsic length metric up to one scale; a homeomorphism alone does not fix it | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy & Whiteley (2025), [LIT-935](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-935.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md). Under Hypothesis 1 (continuous injective ϕ_f from a compact feature space to the sphere) and Hypothesis 2 (CosSim = g(d²) locally, g ∈ C², g′(0) < 0), path lengths scale by √(−2g′(0)). So geodesics on the representation measure the feature, without knowing g. Both hypotheses are assumed, not derived from training. GPT-2's years are homeomorphic to both a linear and a logarithmic scale, and only the metric test told them apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md) | In small CIFAR and MNIST autoencoders whose only basis-privileging primitive is the activation function, elementwise tanh and Leaky-ReLU concentrate latent representations into narrow beams arranged by the activation's discrete symmetry group, even in layers no activation precedes, while their orthogonally equivariant radial counterparts leave them spread, so axis-aligned discreteness there comes from the primitive, not the task | Bird (2025, v4 2026), [LIT-976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-976.md), read in [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md). Autoencoders of width 12–32 and up to three hidden blocks on CIFAR and MNIST, with rotation-equivariant affine maps, initialisation and optimiser. Elementwise tanh (B_n) and Leaky-ReLU (S_n) give beams along or against the basis, or on the ±1 diagonal, and radial tanh and Leaky-ReLU (O(n)) do not. The evidence is density plots, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. The downstream claims, that this causes grandmother neurons, superposition and neural collapse, are untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-297.md) | A bijection between shapes is equivalent to the linear operator it induces on functions; in orthonormal bases a volume-preserving bijection's matrix is orthogonal, and an isometry's commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator, so it maps each eigenspace to the matching eigenspace | Ovsjanikov, Ben-Chen, Solomon, Butscher & Guibas (2012), [LIT-993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-993.md), Remarks 4.1–4.3, Theorem 5.1 with App. A, and §5.1, read in [NOTE-822](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-822.md). Orthogonality was checked; commutation with the Laplacian is cited as well known. All of it assumes a bijection. The operator runs between two different spaces, but the paper gives no structure for a non-invertible or one-way map, and the stability of truncated eigenspaces is cited to Kato, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md) | Structured and translational knowledge-graph embeddings are 0-cochains of a cellular sheaf of vector spaces pulled back from the schema and scored by its Laplacian; since the zero cochain is always a global section, what they learn is a contrastive margin, not the existence of a section | Gebhart, Hansen and Schrater (2021; AISTATS 2023), [LIT-232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-232.md), §4 and Appendices A and C, read in [NOTE-843](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-843.md). A direct identification, covering Structured Embedding, the Unstructured Model, TransE, TransR and RotatE and not bilinear models. That existence of a section is trivial here, and that the only gluing question is whether fixed data extend, is the paper's own remark taken further by the record; it is what separates this use of sheaves from the contextuality line. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-301.md) | The Procrustes distance between regularization-normalized representations and their average linear-decoding distance bound each other only through the participation ratio of the kernel difference: a small Procrustes distance forces a small decoding distance, but not conversely | Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams (2024), [LIT-257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md), Proposition 3 and App. A.1, read in [NOTE-834](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md). With K_X = XG(X)⁻¹Xᵀ/M, α = Tr K_X, β = Tr K_Y and R_Δ the participation ratio of K_X − K_Y, P⁴/R_Δ ≤ E‖Xw* − Yv*‖² ≤ (2(α + β)P² − P⁴)/R_Δ for targets with E[zzᵀ] = I. The Procrustes–Bures equivalence is imported from [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md). Kernels with orthogonal supports show the converse fails: Procrustes distance maximal, decoding distance as small as 2/r. Finite samples, linear readouts only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-303](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-303.md) | A measurement scenario whose compatibility hypergraph is acyclic admits no contextuality: locally consistent context distributions always glue to a global one, so a contextual scenario needs an induced cycle of length at least four | Vorob'ev (1962), as stated in Budroni, Cabello, Gühne, Kleinmann & Larsson (2022), [LIT-263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md), §V.B.2, Eq. 79, and App. A.6, read in [NOTE-844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-844.md). Distributions that agree on overlaps and sit on a hypergraph with the running-intersection property glue, step by step, to one joint distribution. For sharp measurements this means a chordal compatibility graph. So CHSH's square and KCBS's pentagon are the smallest contextual scenarios. Stated and illustrated in the review, not proved there. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md) | In plane Couette and Poiseuille flow the linearized operator is so far from normal that perturbations can grow transiently by O(R) and resonate by O(R²), and operator perturbations of size O(R⁻²) make it eigenvalue-unstable, at Reynolds numbers where eigenvalue analysis predicts stability | Trefethen, Trefethen, Reddy & Driscoll (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md): computed scalings for the linearized shear flows, mostly credited to earlier work and unified through pseudospectra. That transition to turbulence happens by this linear growth plus nonlinear mixing is the paper's conjecture from a 2 × 2 model, and is not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-312.md) | The large-batch InfoNCE loss is the negative HSIC between representations and image identity plus a nonnegative log-mean-exp of the centred critic, so it bounds a kernel dependence loss from above | Li, Pogodin, Sutherland & Gretton (2021), [LIT-248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-248.md), eq. 28 and Theorem B.1, read in [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md). On a finite dataset of N images with one-hot identity labels, the large-batch InfoNCE loss equals −HSIC(Z,Y) + E_Z log E_Z′ exp(k − μ₁) exactly. The second term is nonnegative by Jensen (the record's step), and for a bounded kernel it is at least γHSIC(Z,Z) less a second-order remainder (Theorem B.1, printed with the remainder's sign reversed). It does not say InfoNCE is HSIC, and it says nothing of the finite-batch estimator. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) | With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks | Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md). Σ_p = ∫ϕϕ* dp is uncentred and unit-trace, so p ↦ Σ_p maps distributions to quantum states, and D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q) (Proposition 4(d), Eq. 8). The upper bound is joint convexity, with equality only if k(x,y) = 0 for x ≠ y. The lower bound is monotonicity under a measurement whose outcome law is p smoothed by h(x,y) = ⟨ϕ(x), Σ^{−1/2}ϕ(y)⟩². The O(σ²) gap is shown only for translation-invariant kernels on the torus with Lipschitz densities. It does not cover centred kernels, or similarity measures that compare Gram matrices of representations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-314.md) | Every minimizer of an arbitrary cost on the training outputs plus a strictly increasing function of the RKHS norm lies in the span of the kernel functions at the training points, by the reproducing property and orthogonal decomposition alone | Schölkopf, Herbrich & Smola (2001), [LIT-261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-261.md), Theorem 1 with its proof (eqs. 18–24), read in [NOTE-836](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-836.md) and checked. No convexity of the cost and no Riesz theorem is used; the RKHS is built from the kernel, so the reproducing property holds by construction. The theorem is stated over countable kernel expansions of finite norm, assumes a minimizer exists, and does not cover costs that see f other than through its values at the training points. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md) | For a non-normal linear operator the eigenvalues govern only the long-run limit: a system whose every mode decays can amplify perturbations over finite times, and hold more forced variance, by factors its spectrum does not predict | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). Linear algebra, worked in examples: growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound from below, not above. It holds in a chosen norm, and a norm can always be found that makes the operator normal. It says nothing about whether the growth survives nonlinearity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md) | Time dependence can destabilize a non-normal linear system that is stable at every instant; non-normality is necessary for this, and random variation of the operator destabilizes generically, needing less variation the more non-normal and less damped the mean operator | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Necessity is a one-line bound and the destabilization is shown in explicit examples. Genericity under noise is cited to stochastic stability theory, and the role of non-normality and damping is shown numerically. In the deterministic examples, variation much faster than the transient growth destabilizes nothing. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-338](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-338.md) | For a list searched from the front, where reaching the i-th item costs i, moving each found item to the front costs at most twice what any rule costs on the same sequence, including rules that know the future (four times counting its own moves), a fixed order by access frequency is within no constant factor, and paying to rearrange ahead of need never helps; for paging, no online rule beats the offline optimum by less than n/(n − n_MIN + 1), and LRU meets that bound | Sleator and Tarjan (1985), [LIT-1093](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1093.md), read in [NOTE-903](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-903.md). With no probabilistic assumption, move-to-front on a sequentially scanned list is within 2 of the best algorithm in its class on every sequence, the rival being free to rearrange as it goes and to know the whole future; a list sorted once by frequency, transpose and frequency count are not within any constant; and any algorithm can be replaced by one no more expensive that makes no paid rearrangement (Theorem 3). For paging the online price of not knowing the future is n/(n − n_MIN + 1), the size of fast memory when the memories are equal. It is one list, or one two-level memory, with uniform items: it says nothing about bins, partitions or search that is not a scan. | Active |
| [THEORY-340](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-340.md) | For answering membership in a static set of n keys with the fewest worst-case cell reads, sorted order with binary search is optimal only when the key universe exceeds a Ramsey-number threshold and table cells may hold nothing but stored keys or pointer symbols; it is beaten for small universes, and by two probes once one cell may hold an encoded value | Yao (1981), [LIT-1097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1097.md), read in [NOTE-891](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-891.md). In the setting later called the cell-probe model, where only cells read are counted and both the arrangement and the adaptive search are arbitrary, ⌈lg(n+1)⌉ probes are needed by any scheme whose cells hold only keys of the set or a fixed stock of pointer symbols, once the universe is astronomically large (Theorems 1 and 1′). One probe suffices for m ≤ 2n − 2 (Theorem 2), and with one extra cell holding any value two probes suffice for m ≥ 2^{16n²} (Theorem 3). Building the table is free, so the paper prices lookup only and says nothing about whether sorting pays for itself. | Active |
| [THEORY-348](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md) | When staying in one state costs a fixed amount per request and leaving it costs a fixed one-time price, switching once the extra cost paid for staying equals that price is within 2 of the offline optimum on every request sequence, and no deterministic online rule does better; with a third option the best guaranteed ratio rises to 3 | Karlin, Manasse, Rudolph and Sleator (1988), [LIT-1096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1096.md), read in [NOTE-893](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-893.md). A snoopy cache holding a shared block pays 1 per write to keep it current, or drops it and pays p to fetch it again on a later read. Dropping once the writes charged since the last read have cost p is strongly 2-competitive (Theorems 3.1 and 4.1); with a read- or write-through option the deterministic lower bound is 3 (Theorem 3.3). It is the first competitive analysis of a rent-or-buy decision, though the paper never uses the name, and its instance is when to stop maintaining a copy. Prices are fixed and known, the guarantee is worst case only, stale reads are forbidden rather than priced, and the authors call the practical significance "unclear". | Active |
| [THEORY-352](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-352.md) | A pseudorandom generator exists if and only if a one-way function exists, where both are secure against uniform adversaries and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine, as statements about ensembles indexed by n; the construction from an arbitrary one-way function is only weak-preserving, so security at one length is bought at a much greater one | Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md), with Goldreich's Foundations of Cryptography, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), skimmed in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) from the 1995 draft. Theorem 6.2.2: "There are one-way functions iff there are pseudorandom generators." The hard direction runs one-way function → false entropy generator → pseudoentropy generator → generator, by uniform reductions, with seeds of length n^10 in the direct construction. Adversaries are algorithms; the paper has no circuit version, and that the proof carries over to non-uniform adversaries is the reading's inference, not the paper's statement. Everything is asymptotic. Goldreich states the theorem and does not prove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md) | Computational indistinguishability is strictly coarser than statistical closeness: without any assumption there are ensembles on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform, though none of them is efficiently samplable, and an efficiently samplable pair of this kind exists if a pseudorandom generator does, since its output covers at most 2^n of the 2^l(n) strings; all of it is about ensembles indexed by n, not single pairs of distributions | Goldreich, Foundations of Cryptography vol. 1, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), read in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) (Skimmed, 1995 draft, Chapters 1–3 in full), with Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md). Proposition 3.3 proves by counting that some ensemble far from uniform fools every small circuit; its proof is non-constructive and the ensemble cannot be sampled efficiently. A generator's output is efficiently samplable, indistinguishable from uniform by definition, and statistically far by an image count (§3.3.1). That a samplable such pair exists only if one-way functions do is cited to Goldreich 1990, not read. The book's statistical difference has no factor ½, so it is twice total variation. | Active |
